title: Private VPC: offline bundle validation, dependency graph resolution, and staged canary scenarios
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Context: Customers running Redwood Private in fully isolated VPCs and air-gapped environments require a deterministic, auditable path for operator and image upgrades that does not depend on persistent egress. Existing upgrade acceptance docs focus on network rules and mirrors; we need a concrete PRD for a lightweight offline bundle validation flow plus staged canary scenarios that operators (K8s) can execute with only transient, highly-restricted egress or via pre-staged artifact bundles. Goal: define required inputs, validation checks, dependency resolution steps, failure modes and automatic rollback contract for canary rollouts in private deployments. This ticket is the product-ownership spec for engineering to implement the operator-side validation hooks, the on-disk bundle format, and the canary orchestration playbook for site operators.
scope: In scope: definition of offline bundle format (manifest + signed checksums), dependency graph resolution algorithm (operator, CRDs, sidecars), validation steps (signature, compatibility, resource checks), canary rollout playbook for 1-3 node canaries per cluster, and automated rollback triggers. Out of scope: rewrite of operator install CLI UX and alternate package formats (OCI proxying) — those will be follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Offline bundle manifest format defined and published in Confluence with example bundle (manifest fields, signature envelope, artifact list, and operator compatibility matrix).

Bundle validation shim implemented in operator bootstrap that performs: signature verification, checksum reconciliation, dependency graph resolution (explicit graph or fallback heuristic), Kubernetes resource preflight checks (CRDs present, API versions), and disk-space + node-label constraints — verified via unit tests and integration harness.

A canary orchestration blueprint: (a) staged application of bundle to 1 node (canary) with health probes; (b) automated observation window (configurable); (c) automated rollback on health regressions or critical validation failures; (d) documented manual override steps.

Clear contract for minimal transient egress: operator may make a single outbound request to verify bundle provenance (signed manifest) to a configurable mirror URL OR use local mirror; acceptance tests exist for both zero-egress and one-time provenance-check modes.

Rollout metrics and SLOs captured: canary health pass/fail definitions, max tolerated error-rate increase (e.g., +2% request error rate), and SLA impact windows. Dashboard query examples provided (Prometheus + Console dashboard links).

Backward compatibility matrix: operator must allow rollback to previous bundle and ensure KV cache and model artifact migrations are reversible; migration path described in PRD and validated by an integration smoke test.
design_decisions: Use a signed JSON manifest envelope rather than custom binary to keep validation logic inspectable for customers and auditors.
Prefer explicit dependency graphs in the manifest; fallback to name/version heuristics only if graph absent, to reduce flaky resolution behavior.
Canary size defaults to 1 node but should be configurable per-cluster via the operator CRD.
Validation shim runs in an init container context so it can fail fast before mutating cluster resources.
Provide a 'provenance-check-only' mode that performs signature validation without contacting remote mirrors to support strict zero-egress deployments.
notes: Tradeoffs considered: embedding full dependency graphs increases manifest size but reduces runtime probing and network calls; we prefer explicit graphs to minimize unpredictable resolution in isolated networks. We considered an OCI-only model (pull through mirror) but surfaced the offline bundle approach as lower operational friction for customers with extremely restrictive policies.
